title: OneDrive vs. Google Drive: Which is best? [2026]
summary: Platform preference will definitely influence your choice between OneDrive and Google Drive, but there are some key differences you should know about as well.
body_markdown:
**OneDrive**


**Google Drive**


**Personal plans**


⭐⭐⭐ Modest 5 GB free plan; paid plans start at $1.99/month for 100 GB or $9.99/month for 1 TB


⭐⭐⭐⭐ Generous 15 GB free plan; paid plans start at $1.99/month for 100 GB or $9.99/month for 2 TB


**Business plans**


⭐⭐⭐⭐ 1 TB per user on the $7/user/month Microsoft 365 Business Basic plan


⭐⭐⭐ Google Workspace Business Starter costs $7/user/month, but only includes 30 GB of storage


**Local file syncing**


⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Block-level copying uploads only what's changed instead of the whole file, so file syncs run noticeably faster


⭐⭐⭐ No block-level copying, so syncs take longer, especially with large files


**File search and organization**


⭐⭐⭐ Standard folder hierarchy with filters for file type, date modified, and the user who last modified the file


⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Natural-language search, Boolean operators, and AI overviews within Google Drive that summarize files after you run a search (on higher tier plans)


**Integrations**


⭐⭐⭐⭐ Integrates with the Microsoft ecosystem, but not natively with third-party platforms; connects with thousands of other apps through Zapier


⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Google Workspace Marketplace offers hundreds of native integrations with popular apps; also integrates with thousands of other apps through Zapier


**AI features**


⭐⭐⭐⭐ Copilot summarizes files, compares versions side by side, and answers questions about what's inside a document; OneDrive agents let you create a shareable AI chatbot that draws from specific files


⭐⭐⭐⭐ Gemini lets you hold detailed conversations that take the contents of your Google Drive into account; Gemini Gems make it easier to converse and take action based on the context of multiple files
